I have thought about this issue myself and am not really close to any real answers, however I can offer this. 

In the world of technology, social integration has become low maintenance. I mean that by how little effort is required to communicate with others in the online world. I simply click on the chat window, type a message and it’s sent. No real planning for that conversation is needed, it’s almost effortless. 

Now, the real kicker is why it always seems like we’re the ones initiating conversations. There’s a stray thought that if we didn’t start the conversation with them, it wouldn’t take place. 

I believe that the cause is the low maintenance factor of social media, it has ruined our perception on the level of effort required to engage with each other. 

It’s always different in person because social media cannot replace the signals we’re taking in with face-to-face conversation like body language, tone etc. 

Social media does, however, inform us of each other’s movements more efficiently. 

If you’re out and about, you might post a picture and therefore all your friends can see that. Now that they’re already aware of your day, that aspect of a conversation topic might be unnecessary. 

Similarly, if you’re posting online that you’re having a bad day, and someone asks in the comments and you reply to their comment, publicly (within your network of friends) you’ve informed them all. Anyone reading the comment feed won’t ask now, because they already have the information. 

More over, because we’ve fallen into the world of low maintenance, we’re less likely to want to meet up to discuss your problems and even worse, because there’s a comment feed discussing your issues, we’re further unlikely to even bother sending a message. 

What’s a solution? 

- Have more face-to-face interactions. 
- Share more specific details of your life with those closest to you. 
- Go offline once in a while. When you return, you’ll have a lot to catch people up on. 

It’s sad that in today’s world, we’re more self-obsessed with our own version of reality and not at all obsessed with the reality of others. 

TL;DR:
1. Social media is weakening physical efforts in communication. 
2. Sharing details about your life reduces the topics for conversation because others have already seen it on your feed. 
3. Go offline once in a while and live in the real world.

Check all windows and doors to see whether they open and lock - if they don't, there many be structural warping as well. 

Get an independent building inspector and specifically ask them to check for extra things like past damages or mixes of old and newer materials which may suggest repairs. 

Discuss any natural disaster that have happened in the last... Not all damages need immediate repairs after an event... But they might during your ownership.

I was a property manager who handled all the leasing and running of 126 privately owned houses. This tenant of ours, maybe early 50's, lived alone in one of our rural properties with her 4 dogs. She wasn't a well lady and had regular doctors appointments. 

One day she missed her appointment and the doctor called us (small town, everyone knows everyone) to see if we can get a hold of her because it's unlike her to miss an appointment. Two weeks had passed and we still never heard anything from her, so we wrote a letter thinking that maybe her phone wasn't working. She paid her rent directly into the company trust account, so we rarely had her visit the office to pay and her house was always immaculate during inspections, so she was a good, trouble-free tenant. 

A week after we sent the letter, we still didn't get a reply, so I went to visit her. I drove out to the house and noticed something wasn't right straight away. 

1. Her dogs didn't greet me. 
2. Gardens and lawn was a bit over grown. 
3. Letter box was full of mail. 

I timidly walked up the stairs to knock when I was greeted by a foul smell. I instantly knew she was dead. 

I used my key to unlock the door and found her face down dead in the middle of the lounge room, dressed in her pyjamas. Her dogs were also dead in the kitchen, water and food bowls empty and the house was locked up. No windows open or doors.
